_comment: senechal's typed front doors: the machine-readable contract `notify-senechal` files against, published here and FETCHED at call time rather than hardcoded in the caller. WHY (2026-08-16): the front door took free text and produced a prose GitHub issue, while every consumer downstream (health/dead-config.sh, health/hosts-unregistered.sh) reads structure -- so every filing needed a human to translate prose into schema, and health/unabsorbed-notices.sh existed only to nag about the backlog of untranslated prose. The note already knows its type at the call site: remedies/window-spawn-desktop.sh files a footprint record flattened into a sentence, then re-parsed by a human days later. A door makes that round trip unnecessary. Ownership: realisateur owns THAT doors exist and how the command is distributed; senechal owns WHAT EACH DOOR REQUIRES, i.e. this file -- so senechal can add a door without an edit in realisateur's repo. That seam is not theoretical: notify-senechal's filing footer is a senechal contract hardcoded in realisateur, and dropping it took tools/issue-janitor.py BLIND for a day (senechal#221).
_transport_comment: The transport stays a GitHub issue, because the live config is ~/.config/senechal/senechal.json on one host and a caller on `monkey` has neither a clone nor write access -- that constraint is what put prose in an issue in the first place, and it has not changed. What changes is the LETTER, not the mail slot: a fenced ```senechal-door block carrying a validated object, which tools/absorb-notices.py applies to the live config unattended. Label `door` is how the absorber finds them; `idea` stays on for continuity with issue-janitor.py's gates.
_no_prose_door_comment: There is deliberately no free-text door. If no door fits what an agent needs to file, the fix is to ADD ONE -- a PR to this file plus its apply rule in tools/absorb-notices.py -- not to fall back to a paragraph. A prose fallback would always be the path of least resistance, and every filing would take it, which is exactly the state this replaces.

footprint.comment: Something a project installed on a host that outlives the session that installed it. Lands in estate.footprint, probed thereafter by health/dead-config.sh.

help.id: stable slug, unique in the registry, e.g. crt-whisper-server
help.target: kind-specific: unit name, port number, or absolute path
help.host: which device in estate.devices it is installed on
help.owner: the project that fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.retire: the exact command that finishes removing it
help.notes: why it exists, and what its removal is waiting on

crontab.comment: A crontab entry another project's own account added on a host, so the change is senechal-visible instead of arriving as a hand-filed prose issue (hf7y/senechal#362, the second time this exact filing had no typed door to land in). Lands in estate.crontab, a separate registry from estate.footprint because footprint's target is restricted to a unit name, port number or absolute path and cannot carry a schedule or a command line.

help.tag: the trailing `# <owner>:<mechanism>:TICK` comment identifying the line, unique in the registry
help.host: which device in estate.devices the crontab lives on
help.account: the UNIX account whose crontab this is -- not necessarily the same as owner
help.owner: the project that owns this cron entry and fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.command: the command line, including any inline env vars
help.retire: the exact command that removes this line, e.g. crontab -l | grep -v '<tag>' | crontab -
help.notes: why it exists, where a backup of the prior crontab was made, and what it writes

verb.comment: A verb `installe` put on PATH, so an install lands in estate.verbs instead of failing UNDECLARED (hf7y/senechal#414: this door did not exist, so every `installe verb` call ever filed one). Lands in estate.verbs, a separate registry from estate.footprint because footprint's target is restricted to a unit name, port number or absolute path and cannot carry which project owns the verb or which build it is pinned to -- the facts worth registering, per #414.

help.name: the verb's bare name, as it lands on PATH
help.host: which device in estate.devices it is installed on
help.account: the UNIX account whose ~/.local/bin or /usr/local/bin holds it
help.project: the project that owns the verb and fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.build: the build id the link is pinned to, e.g. 2026-08-24T033024Z
help.retire: the exact command that removes it: installe retire <name>

device.comment: A machine senechal did not know about. Lands in estate.devices, after which every health check covers it, because they read this list and never their own host list.

help.name: short hostname, e.g. monkey
help.addr: how to reach it: localhost, an ssh host, or a .local name
help.expect: always-on | intermittent -- what an unreachable probe means
help.owner: who fixes problems in that device's domain
help.notes: what it is for, and what runs on it
